LVKE.|141}}</noinclude>should not see death vnles he savv first the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''See John 1, 20. and 41.''}}* {{sc|Christ}} of our Lord. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=27}}† And he came in spirit into the temple. And vvhen his parents brought in the childe {{sc|Iesvs}}, to doe according to the custome of the Lavv for him: {{verse|chapter=2|verse=28}}† he also tooke him into his armes, and blessed God, and said,

{{verse|chapter=2|verse=29}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ NVNC DIMITTIS at Complin.}}∷ ''{{sc|Now thov}} doest dimisse thy seruant O Lord, according to thy vvord in peace''. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=30}}† ''Because mine eies haue seen, thy Salvation,'' {{verse|chapter=2|verse=31}}† ''Which thou hast prepared before the face of al peoples'':

{{verse|chapter=2|verse=32}}† ''A light to the reuelation of the Gentils, and the glorie of thy people Israel''.⊣

{{verse|chapter=2|verse=33}}† And his father and mother vvere marueling vpon those things vvhich vvere spoken concerning him. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=34}}† And Simeon blessed them, and said to {{sc|Marie}} his mother, Behold this is set vn{{sup|‖}} to the ruine, and vnto the resurrection of many in Israel, and for a signe vvhich shal be contradicted, {{verse|chapter=2|verse=35}}† and {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Simeon prophecied not only of Christ but of our B. Lady, of al her sorowes: wherein she was alwaies partaker with our Sauiour, from his flight into Ægypt euen to his death.}}∷ thine ovvne soule shal a sword pearce, that out of many hartes cogitations may be reuealed. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=36}}† And there vvas Anne a prophetisse, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Aser: she was farre striken in daies, and had liued vvith her husband seuen yeres from her virginitie. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=37}}† And she vvas {{sup|‖}} a vvidovv vntil eightie and foure yeres: vvho departed not from the temple, {{sup|‖}} by fastings and praiers {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''λατρέυουσα.''}}∷ seruing night and day. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=38}}† And she at the same houre sodenly comming in, confessed to our Lord: and spake of him to al that expected the redemption of Israel. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=39}}† And after they had vvholy done al things according to the lavv of our Lord, they returned into Galilee, into their citie Nazareth.

{{verse|chapter=2|verse=40}}† And the childe grevv, and vvaxed {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''`strong in spirit'':}}`strong': ful of wisedom, and the grace of God vvas in him. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=41}}† And his parents vvent euery yere vnto Hierusalem, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 23, 15. 34, 17. Deu. 16, 1.''}}* at the solemne day of Pasche. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=42}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō the first Sunday after the Epiphanie.}}And vvhen he vvas tvvelue yeres old, they going vp into Hierusalem according to the custome of the festiual day, {{verse|chapter=2|verse=43}}† and hauing ended the daies, vvhen they returned, the childe {{sc|Iesvs}} remained in Hierusalem: and his parents knew it not. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=44}}† And thinking that he vvas in the companie, they came a daies iourney, and sought him among their kinsfolke and acquaintance. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=45}}† And not finding him, they returned into Hierusalem, seeking him. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=46}}† And it came to passe, after three daies they found him in the temple sitting in the middes of the Doctors, hearing them, and asking them. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=47}}† And al vvere astonied that heard him, vpon his vvisedom and ansvvers.<noinclude>{{rh||S iij|And}}</noinclude>
